reference-doc.md && sed -n '2375,2535p' reference-doc.md\"", "aggregated_output": "\n`eval run --file` reads the versioned suite f
ile (`schemaVersion: \"1\"`),\nauthenticates, then validates. A contract-invalid file exits **2** after the\nauth request — it doe

s not start a run. `eval validate` on the same bytes
still exits 1: that command is a verdict on the file; this one is not.

Th
e file's `suite.id` is the declared suite identity. The first run creates a\nfile-owned suite stamped with that id; later runs of
the same id in the same\nproject update that suite rather than creating a second one. A UI-authored\nsuite has no declared id, so

no file can claim it. Resolve is never by name.

File `passThreshold` is a fraction; the hosted suite grades on a percent. The
conversion refuses rather than approximates. A file count above **10**\n(`repetitions` in a `schemaVersion: \"1\"` file, `iteratio

ns` in `"2"`) is
refused by name (`REPETITIONS_CAP`) and is not clamped.

**Which vocabulary the sync speaks is the deploymen
t's call.** Before writing\nanything, the CLI reads `GET /capabilities` once. A deployment that advertises\n`vocabulary.version: 2
` gets every request with `x-mcpjam-eval-vocabulary: 2`\nand case bodies spelled canonically — `iterations` (the exact count),\n`l
egacyIterations` (the legacy floor, the same number) and `assertions` —\ninstead of `repetitions` / `iterations` / `checks`. A dep
loyment without the\ncapability block, or without the capabilities route at all, is spoken to in\nvocabulary 1, byte-for-byte as b

efore. Nothing in the file changes either way:
the dialect of the file and the vocabulary of the wire are independent.

Cases a
re synced in batches of at most 100 (`create_eval_cases`). Every\ndeclared case is created or updated, including `disabled: true`
rows. A case\nthe file **no longer declares** is deleted from the hosted suite before\nlaunch. A case the file still declares but
marks `disabled: true` is **kept,\nwith its history** — it is simply left out of the launch, so parking a flaky\ntest does not des
troy its past results and re-enabling it later resumes the\nsame case.\nThe run is scoped to the enabled cases either way. A file
with no enabled\ncases is refused (`NO_ENABLED_CASES`) rather than launching the whole\npersisted suite. `--case` may only name an
